headline: Steady revenue growth, profit falls on merger costs
summary_short: Iridium's Q2 2026 revenue rose 3.8% y/y to $225M on commercial and government service growth, while net income fell to $9.7M (-55.9% y/y) and diluted EPS to $0.09 as $14.3M of transaction costs tied to the pending Rocket Lab acquisition weighed on results.
summary_long: Revenue rose 3.8% y/y to $225M on 4% commercial service growth (IoT +5% on subscribers, hosted payload +14%) and 3% government service growth on EMSS rate increases. Net income fell to $9.7M (-55.9% y/y) and diluted EPS to $0.09, which the company says was primarily due to increases in transaction costs; $14.3M of transaction-related expenses hit Q2 2026 versus none a year ago, tied to the pending Rocket Lab acquisition and the since-closed Aireon deal. OEBITDA of $119.1M was down 2% y/y on a $3.9M rise in cash-paid incentive comp. Cash rose to $184.2M (+65.0% q/q); no reason is given. The company will not hold earnings calls or give guidance while the Rocket Lab deal is pending.

drivers.explanation: Iridium will not hold conference calls or update/provide guidance while its pending acquisition by Rocket Lab (announced June 28, 2026, expected to close mid-2027) is outstanding; it separately closed its previously announced Aireon acquisition on July 2, 2026.
Commercial service revenue grew 4% on IoT subscriber growth (+9% billable subscribers) and hosted-payload/other growth; government service grew 3% on contractual EMSS rate increases.
Revenue grew 3.8% y/y while combined cost of services and subscriber-equipment costs were roughly flat (-0.2%), so nearly all of the revenue gain flowed through to gross profit.
SG&A rose $22.4M y/y to $67.0M, which the OEBITDA reconciliation shows was driven mostly by $14.3M of transaction-related expenses (versus zero a year ago) tied to pending/closed acquisitions.
"The decrease was primarily the result of increases in transaction costs," per the release, referring to M&A-related expenses recognized in the quarter.
Diluted EPS fell in line with net income's 55.9% y/y decline since weighted diluted shares were nearly flat (+0.3% y/y).

This shard's plain EBITDA figure differs from the company's own non-GAAP OEBITDA ($119.1M, -2% y/y), which excludes share-based comp, transaction costs, and equity-method losses that are included here.
Not explained in the release — the filing states the quarter-end cash balance and net debt but gives no narrative for the sequential cash increase.
